subject: Urgent: Acme — US-WEST saturation and planned cross-region switchover
body:
Message 1 (original customer alert)
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: ops+oncall@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency + 5xx spike in US-WEST (sierra AZ) — urgent

Stephanie —

We started seeing sustained tail latency and a 12% 5xx rate across our API calls at ~08:45 PST this morning. Internal retries are amplifying traffic and our downstream ingestion is queueing up. This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers in west coast load zones.

Attached: small error snippet from our client side that shows a consistent 503 with retry headers. Can you confirm whether this is an application issue or a regional infrastructure problem on Redwood's side? We need ETA for mitigation — customers are already escalating.

Thanks,
Jane Doe
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

---

Message 2 (internal triage and routing)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike in US-WEST (sierra AZ) — urgent

Marissa / Rishi / Vanessa —

Got the alert from Acme (see below). Summary: beginning ~08:40 PST we see a sustained increase in tail latency and 5xx rate originating from the Sierra AZ (us-west-2a). Early indicators point to a capacity saturation event on a subset of Dedicated nodes handling Acme's reserved pools (we have correlated increased queue depth and token render backlog).

Immediate ask: Rishi, can you validate whether the affected nodes are on the Dedicated pool for ACME-2027 and confirm whether cross-region-compatible model variants are warm in US-EAST? If yes, propose a switchover plan with timing and rollback.

Marissa, I need an exec note that outlines SLA impact and ask for temporary authorization to reroute a percentage of traffic to us-east while we drain and remediate. This will be an SLA exception for 90 minutes max. Vanessa, prep the customer comms template (short transparent note + canary notice).

Attachments: quick KPI snapshot (token latency histogram) attached for context.

Planning to propose an initial 20% traffic diversion at t+20 minutes, observe, then scale to 60% if metrices stabilize.

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

---

Message 3 (technical breakdown)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike in US-WEST (sierra AZ) — urgent

Stephanie —

I pulled traces and host metrics. Findings: (1) GPU memory pressure on four shard hosts (r5g) leading to queue backpressure, (2) sudden inbound burst from a client-side retry loop amplified by one of their front-end versions, (3) autoscaler for Dedicated pool didn't react fast enough due to burst smoothing threshold.

Mitigation steps (proposed):
- Immediate: enable routing override to send 25% of ACME-2027 traffic to US-EAST (us-east-1) model variant (compatible quantization + same model version). This is a soft-failover routed at the edge, no model spin-up required; estimated 3 minutes to start seeing traffic shift.
- Short window (t+30): if 5xx drops below 1% and p95 latency < 450ms for 15m, increase diversion to 65%.
- If errors persist: escalate to full region drain and a dedicated capacity burst from Dedicated pool (we have warm nodes in west fallback pool, but that requires 18–25 minutes to scale).
- Rollback: edge routing disabled and traffic returns to normal; we keep a 1-hour post-mortem hold.

I attached the runbook snippet for the switchover steps and the quick telemetry snapshot.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

---

Message 4 (customer-facing exec summary + approvals)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike in US-WEST (sierra AZ) — urgent

Jane —

Thanks for flagging and for the snippet you attached — that helped pinpoint the client retry amplification. Quick update and plan (executive summary):

What happened: ~08:40 PST an orchestrated retry pattern from a front-end release at Acme amplified traffic into the Sierra AZ Dedicated pool. Four shard hosts entered memory pressure and queueing, producing 5xx responses as backlog grew.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:05 PST: SRE triage — identified host-level pressure and retry amplification.
- 09:15 PST: We enabled a 25% edge diversion to us-east (soft switchover) to arrest error rates and reduce tail latency. Initial telemetry showed immediate drop in 5xx to ~1.8%.
- 09:45 PST: Increased diversion to 65% after 30m of stable p95 and error rate reduction.
- 10:25 PST: Full drain of affected hosts completed; autoscaler applied burst capacity to replace degraded shards.

Current status (as of this message):
- Error rate: 0.6% 5xx for Acme traffic; p95 latency 310ms; throughput at expected levels.
- We completed host remediation and verified model variant integrity.

Next steps for Acme:
- We recommend a short front-end rollback on your side for the retry behavior patch to prevent recurrence.
- Redwood will provide a detailed post-mortem and telemetry dump within 48 hours.
- We will issue a service credit for the impacted window consistent with our SLA; Marissa will follow up on the credit calculation and approval route.

If you need a call to walk through the timeline and telemetry, I can join with Rishi and Vanessa at 14:00 PST today.

Apologies for the disruption — we treated this as a P1 and prioritized routing controls and safety-first rollbacks to protect customer traffic.

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182
